mainTopic: Penalties for improper sales, and how the price is calculated when a sold field or an עבד עברי is redeemed
overview: The עמוד opens by explaining why רב ענן still had a doubt about a field sold during the יובל year. He had not heard the ברייתא, and שמואל's ruling could mean the money is returned or is a gift, as in the case of המקדש אחותו. Next, אביי and רב יוסף discuss a slave sold to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל. Using the picture of a mouse and its hole, they conclude that the penalty falls on whoever now holds the forbidden item. The גמרא then explains two lines of the משנה: why a plowed year counts for the buyer, and רבי אליעזר's rule that a buyer can eat three crops in two years. A new משנה teaches that when a field was resold, the owner redeems it by the lower price, and it lists ways of raising redemption money that are forbidden with an ordinary buyer but allowed with הקדש. In the גמרא, רבי and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה read the פסוק in two different ways that both help the seller, and the גמרא shows the case where they differ. It explains that redemption is read leniently because of a גזירה שוה with the redemption of an עבד עברי, who always pays by the lower value. The עמוד ends as אביי begins a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why רב ענן still had a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב ענן did not know the ברייתא. It also explains that שמואל's ruling could not settle his question, because it can be read two ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן never heard the ברייתא. As for שמואל's statement, how do we know he meant 'the field is not sold and the money goes back'? Maybe he meant 'the field is not sold and the money is a gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: why did רב ענן ask about a sale during יובל when there were sources that could answer him? It says he did not know the ברייתא, and שמואל's words were unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said the field is 'not sold.' That leaves the money open. It could go back to the buyer, or it could be treated as a gift to the seller. Because of this ambiguity, שמואל's ruling could not settle רב ענן's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
He had not heard it; he did not know this source
From where do we know? How can we be sure?
It (the field) is not sold; the sale does not take effect
The money goes back to the buyer
Perhaps; maybe it means something else

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב עָנָן בָּרָיְיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And Rav Anan had not heard the baraita,
and as for Shmuel's statement, from where do we know
phrases.notes: שמואל had said that a field sold during the יובל year is not sold.

phrases.english: that it is not sold and the money goes back?
Perhaps it is not sold and the money is a gift,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב עָנָן בָּרָיְיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רב ענן's question about a sale during יובל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source was unknown, and the other source is ambiguous
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ענן should have been able to settle his doubt from the ברייתא or from שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not know the ברייתא, and שמואל's words can also mean that the money is a gift

steps.title: שמואל's view on a man who betroths his sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שמואל elsewhere holds that money given in a deal that cannot take effect is treated as a gift. This is the case of המקדש אחותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like one who betroths his sister. As it was stated: one who betroths his sister — רב says the money goes back, and שמואל says the money is a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the 'gift' reading of שמואל. It points to another case where שמואל clearly says the money is a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothal to one's sister cannot take effect. So what happens to the money he gave her? שמואל says it is a gift, because the man knew the betrothal would not work. This shows שמואל could hold the same way about a sale during יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; a comparison to a similar case
One who betroths his own sister, a betrothal that cannot take effect
The money is treated as a gift

phrases.english: just as it is with one who betroths his sister,
as it was stated: one who betroths his sister —
Rav says: the money goes back,
and Shmuel says: the money is a gift.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'not sold' does not tell us what happens to the money. Since he says in the case of המקדש אחותו that the money is a gift, רב ענן could not use שמואל to settle his question.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'gift' reading suggested in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל might hold the money is a gift
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about המקדש אחותו

steps.title: Why penalize the buyer and not the seller?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף why, when a slave is sold outside ארץ ישראל, the buyer is the one who loses.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What makes you penalize the buyer? Let us penalize the seller!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges a ruling taught earlier: when a slave is sold outside ארץ ישראל, the buyer must free him and does not get his money back. אביי asks why the seller should not be the one penalized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this ruling, the buyer loses both the slave and his money, while the seller keeps the money. אביי argues that the seller did the wrong act of selling, so he should be the one penalized by having to return the money.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this side over the other?
We penalize; the רבנן impose a קנס (fine)
The buyer
The seller

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What did you see that we penalize the buyer?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the slave sold to someone outside ארץ ישראל: the buyer must free him and loses his money.

phrases.english: Let us penalize the seller!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the penalty for selling a slave outside ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the buyer loses his money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller started the forbidden sale, so he seems more fitting to penalize

steps.title: The hole steals, not the mouse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with a parable: the real thief is the hole, not the mouse. This means the buyer is the one who makes the wrong possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not the mouse that steals; rather, the hole steals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends penalizing the buyer by using a picture of a mouse and its hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mouse cannot steal unless it has a hole to hide the food in. In the same way, the seller could not sell the slave outside ארץ ישראל if no buyer were willing to take him. So the buyer is the one who makes the wrongdoing possible.

keyTerms.meaning: A mouse; here it stands for the seller
A hole; here it stands for the buyer
Steals; the thief

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not the mouse that steals,
rather, the hole steals.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו עַכְבְּרָא גַּנָּב, אֶלָּא חוֹרָא גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parable showing who makes the wrong possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller is the main wrongdoer
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer, like the hole, is what makes the wrong possible

steps.title: Without the mouse, the hole gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns the parable around: without the mouse, the hole would have nothing to hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the mouse, where would the hole get anything from?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back using רב יוסף's own picture. The seller is just as necessary as the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hole only holds stolen food because the mouse brings it. In the same way, the buyer could only take the slave out because the seller sold him. So the parable does not show that the buyer is more at fault.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for
From where would it get it?

phrases.english: If not for the mouse,
where would the hole get it from?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו עַכְבְּרָא, חוֹרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the parable in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sides are needed for the wrong, so the parable does not single out the buyer

steps.title: Penalize where the forbidden item is
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף concludes that the penalty falls on whoever now holds the forbidden item, which is the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason: wherever the forbidden thing is, that is where we impose the penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the final reason for penalizing the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that both sides share the blame. The deciding factor is that the slave is now with the buyer. The penalty is placed where the forbidden item actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it is logical
Wherever it is found
The forbidden thing; here, the slave taken out of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: It stands to reason: wherever the forbidden thing is, there we penalize.

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל, the buyer is penalized. The reason is not that he is more guilty, but that the forbidden item (the slave) is now in his hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for where the רבנן place a קנס when two parties share in a wrong: on the one who now holds the forbidden item.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the back-and-forth over the parable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both sides share the blame, the parable cannot decide
steps.terutzMaskana: The penalty goes where the forbidden item now is: the buyer

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention plowing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a שנת שדפון and asks why plowing needs to be mentioned if a fallow year already counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If it was a year of blight, etc.' Now, if leaving it fallow counts for him, is it necessary to say that plowing it counts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the opening words as a setup, then asks why one of its cases seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a year counts toward the buyer's years even if he only plowed the field, or even if he left it fallow. If leaving it completely unworked counts, then a year when he at least plowed should obviously count. So why does the משנה bother to mention plowing?

keyTerms.meaning: A year of blight, when crops are ruined
He left it fallow, without working it
He plowed it but did not sow it
Now, since this is so
Is it necessary to say?

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first words of the משנה ('a year of blight') are quoted here. The question is about a later part of that same משנה: the cases of plowing and leaving the field fallow.

phrases.english: If it was a year of blight, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: a year he plowed or left fallow still counts.

phrases.english: Now, if leaving it fallow counts for him,
is it necessary to say that plowing it counts?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא הוֹבִירָהּ עוֹלָה לוֹ, נָרָהּ מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the slave discussion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bigger case (fallow) counts, the smaller case (plowed) is obvious and should not need to be said

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to mention plowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that plowing had to be mentioned. Otherwise we might think the owner can pay the buyer for his plowing work and take the field back early.
steps.simpleTranslation: Plowing had to be mentioned. You might have thought we tell the owner: 'Pay the buyer for the value of his plowing, and he leaves.' The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7. It explains why the משנה mentions a year in which the buyer plowed the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the buyer plowed, he put work into the field. So we might think the owner could simply pay him for that work and take the field back, and the year would not count. The משנה teaches that this is wrong: the plowed year counts as one of the buyer's years, and the owner cannot buy him out.

keyTerms.meaning: He plowed it (broke up the soil) but did not plant
You might have thought (the wrong first idea)
Give him its value (pay him for his work)
It teaches us (that the first idea is wrong)

phrases.english: Plowed it — it was necessary for him [to teach],
since it would enter your mind to say
that we say to him:
Give him its value, and let him leave,
phrases.notes: The owner would pay the buyer for the work he put into plowing, and then the buyer would leave the field.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7 about why plowing needs to be mentioned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that the extra case is needed to block a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the buyer worked the land, the owner could pay him for the plowing and take the field back early.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plowed year counts toward the buyer's years. The owner cannot buy him out by paying for the plowing.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a field sold full of produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר from the משנה and brings a ברייתא. It asks how we know that the seller cannot demand the field back full of produce, the way he handed it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר says, if he sold it to him, etc. A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, how do we know that if he sold the field before ראש השנה full of produce, the seller may not say to the buyer, 'Leave it for me full of produce, the way I left it for you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, the words of רבי אליעזר. It brings a ברייתא that asks for the source of his rule, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field was handed over full of crops, so the buyer got an extra harvest. It would seem fair for the seller to say, 'Give it back the same way, full of crops.' The ברייתא asks where we learn that the seller cannot demand this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (how do we know this from the Torah)?
The new year; here the field was sold just before it, already full of crops
Full of produce (crops already growing in it)
Leave [it] for me (give it back in the same condition)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he sold it to him, etc.
It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From where [do we know] that if he sold it to him
before Rosh HaShana, full of produce,
that he may not say to him:
'Leave [it] for me the way I left [it] for you'?
phrases.notes: The seller is the one speaking here. He wants the field back full of crops, just as it was when he sold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם מְכָרָהּ לוֹ לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מְלֵיאָה פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that the seller cannot demand the field back full of produce.

steps.title: The verse counts years, not crops
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק 'according to the number of years of crops.' The sale is counted in years, so a buyer may sometimes eat three crops in two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.' So sometimes a person eats three crops in two years.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק. The sale is measured by years, not by the number of harvests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the sale goes by the 'number of years.' So the buyer is owed two full years of use, not exactly two harvests. If he received the field already full of crops, he keeps that extra harvest and does not have to return the field full of crops.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the Torah source)
Years of crops: the sale is counted in years
Crops, harvests

steps.whatToRemember: A field sale is counted by years, not by harvests. So a buyer who received the field full of crops can end up with three harvests in two years.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:15

phrases.english: sometimes a person eats
three crops in two years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says 'number of years,' so the sale is counted in years, and the buyer may sometimes eat three crops in two years.

steps.title: Resold for more: the owner pays the first price
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the first buyer resold the field for a higher price, the original owner works out the redemption only by the first, lower price.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the owner sold the field to the first buyer for a מנה (100), and the first buyer sold it to a second buyer for 200, the owner calculates only with the first buyer's price. As the פסוק says: 'to whom he sold it.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a field that was sold, then resold for more money, and asks which price the owner uses when he buys it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner redeems the field, he pays back part of the sale price, based on the years that are left. The משנה says he goes by the price he himself received, 100, and not by the 200 the second buyer paid. The proof is the words 'to whom he sold it,' meaning the person the owner himself sold to.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה starts here)
A מנה, which is 100 דינרים
Calculates (works out how much to pay back for the years that are left)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he sold it to the first [buyer] for a maneh (100),
and the first sold [it] to the second for two hundred,
he calculates only with the first,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the original owner who is buying the field back. He uses the price the first buyer paid him.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'to whom he sold it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:27

steps.triggerLanguage: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָנֶה, וּמָכַר רִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that opens a new topic: redeeming a field that was resold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the field was resold for more, the owner redeems it based on the first, lower price.

steps.title: Resold for less: the owner pays the last price
steps.stepSummary: If the first buyer resold the field for less, the owner works out the redemption by the last, lower price. The proof is the extra words 'to the man,' meaning the man who holds the field now.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner sold the field to the first buyer for 200, and the first buyer sold it to the second for a מנה (100), the owner calculates only with the last buyer's price. As the פסוק says: 'And he shall calculate the years of its sale and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it.' 'To the man' means the man who is in it now.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case, where the field was resold for less. Here the owner goes by the last buyer's price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reads the words 'to the man' as pointing to whoever is in the field now, which is the second buyer. So the owner calculates with the 100 that the last buyer paid. The same פסוק gives the rule in both cases, and the result is that the owner always pays by the lower price.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder: the part of the price that matches the years still left
Who is in it: the person holding the field right now
Its sale

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect one fixed rule like 'always the first buyer' or 'always the last buyer.' The משנה reads the פסוק in a way that, in both cases, has the owner pay by the lower price.
steps.whatToRemember: With a resold field, the owner redeems by the lower of the two prices. If the resale was for more, he uses the first price ('to whom he sold it'). If the resale was for less, he uses the last price ('to the man,' the one in it now).

phrases.english: If he sold it to the first for two hundred,
and the first sold [it] to the second for a maneh (100),
he calculates only with the last,
as it is stated: 'And he shall calculate the years of its sale
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:27

phrases.english: and return the remainder
to the man to whom he sold it,'
to the man who is in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָאתַיִם, וּמָכַר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case to Step 11, learned from a different part of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the field was resold for less, the owner redeems it based on the last buyer's lower price, since 'to the man' means the one holding the field now.

steps.title: Ways the seller may not raise money to redeem his field
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists ways the seller may not get the money to redeem his field: selling a far field to redeem a near one, selling a poor field to redeem a good one, borrowing, or redeeming half at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not sell a far field and redeem a near one, or sell a bad field and redeem a good one. He may not borrow money and redeem, and he may not redeem in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rules about redeeming a sold field. It now lists four ways of redeeming that are not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four cases are ways of putting together the redemption money other than paying the full price from his own funds at one time. Two involve selling another field, one involves a loan, and one involves paying in parts. The משנה says none of these is allowed when redeeming from an ordinary buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that is far away / a field that is nearby
A poor-quality field / a good-quality field
He will borrow money
In halves, paying part now and part later

phrases.english: He may not sell a distant field and redeem a nearby one,
or sell a poor field and redeem a good one,
phrases.notes: The words 'he may not sell' from the first line carry over to this one.

phrases.english: and he may not borrow and redeem,
and he may not redeem in halves,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules for redeeming a sold field, moving from how the price is worked out to how the money may be raised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller may not redeem his field by selling a far or poor field, by borrowing, or by paying in halves.

steps.title: With הקדש all these ways are allowed
steps.stepSummary: When redeeming a field from הקדש, every one of these ways is allowed. So in this rule an ordinary person's field is treated more strictly than הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: With הקדש, all of these are allowed. This is a case where the law is stricter for an ordinary person than for הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by comparing these limits to redeeming a field from הקדש. There, all four ways are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually הקדש gets stricter rules than ordinary property. Here it is the other way around. The limits on redeeming apply only to a field sold to an ordinary person, not to a field given to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
A stricter rule
An ordinary person, not הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume הקדש is always the stricter side. In this rule the ordinary person's field is the stricter one.
steps.whatToRemember: Selling another field, borrowing, and paying in halves are not allowed when redeeming from an ordinary buyer, but they are allowed when redeeming from הקדש.

phrases.english: But with הקדש, all of them are permitted.
This is a stringency for an ordinary person more than for הקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה by contrasting the limits in step 13 with הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the limits on redeeming apply to an ordinary buyer and not to הקדש, so here the ordinary person's field is treated more strictly.

steps.title: Source for paying by the first price when the field was resold for more
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks for the source of the rule that if the field was sold for 100 and then resold for 200, the seller pays according to the first sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sold it to the first buyer for 100, and the first buyer sold it to a second buyer for 200. How do we know he works out the price only with the first buyer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that looks for the source of the משנה's rule from step 11. Here it sets up the question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a resale for a higher price. The ברייתא wants a פסוק showing that the seller does not have to pay the second, higher price.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth 100 דינרים
Works out (the redemption price)
From where do we know?

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
If he sold it to the first buyer for a מנה (100),
and the first sold it to the second for 200,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: from where do we know that he calculates only with the first?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the source of the step 11 rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that after a resale for more, the seller pays by the first, lower price.

steps.title: The answer: 'to whom he sold it'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the seller returns the money 'to the man to whom he sold it,' meaning the first buyer, so the first sale's price is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'to the man to whom he sold it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with words from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller sold the field to the first buyer, not to the second. Since the פסוק ties the payment to the one he sold to, the first, lower price is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
To whom he sold it

phrases.english: The verse states: '[to the man] to whom he sold it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:27. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, filling in the full פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'To whom he sold it' points to the first buyer, so the first price is used.

steps.title: Source for paying by the second price when the field was resold for less
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks for a source for the opposite case: sold for 200, then resold for 100. How do we know the price is worked out with the second buyer?
steps.simpleTranslation: He sold it to the first buyer for 200, and the first sold it to the second for 100. How do we know the price is worked out only with the second?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns to the reverse case from step 12 and asks for its source. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the second price is lower. The ברייתא wants a source for using it, even though the פסוק just quoted seemed to point to the first buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hundred דינרים
The second buyer

phrases.english: If he sold it to the first for 200,
and the first sold it to the second for a מנה (100),

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא עִם הַשֵּׁנִי?
phrases.english: from where do we know that the calculation is only with the second?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא עִם הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 15, now for the reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that after a resale for less, the seller pays by the second, lower price.

steps.title: The answer: 'to the man,' the one who holds the field now
steps.stepSummary: The extra words 'to the man' are read as 'to the man who is in it,' the one holding the field now. This is the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'to the man,' meaning to the man who is in it. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words 'to the man' and says this is רבי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'to whom he sold it.' The extra 'to the man' teaches that payment can also follow whoever now holds the field. Put together, the seller always pays by the lower of the two prices.

keyTerms.meaning: To the man
Who is in it, the one holding the field now

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, the seller pays by the lower price: 'to whom he sold it' covers a resale for more, and 'to the man' covers a resale for less.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'to the man' — to the man who is in it,
phrases.notes: The first 'to the man' quotes the פסוק. The repeat in square brackets is the corrected wording and starts the explanation: the man now on the field.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: לָאִישׁ לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 and names רבי as the author of this reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'to the man' means the one holding the field now, so the second, lower price is used.

steps.title: רבי דוסתאי's case: the field rose in value
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה brings a different case: the field was sold for 100 and rose in value to 200 while the buyer held it. How do we know the seller pays only 100?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says: He sold it to him for 100, and it improved and became worth 200. How do we know he works out the price only by the 100?
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different reading of the same פסוק. He first sets up his case and question; his source comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no second buyer. The field simply became more valuable. The question is whether the seller pays by today's value or by the original price.

keyTerms.meaning: It improved, rose in value
It came to be worth

phrases.english: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says:
If he sold it to him for a מנה (100),
and it improved and came to be worth 200,
from where do we know that he calculates only by the מנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to read the פסוק that רבי used, applying it to a field that rose in value.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a rise in the field's value does not raise the redemption price.

steps.title: The answer: 'the remainder' that is in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'and he returns the remainder,' meaning what is left of the money he actually received. So he pays only by the original 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he returns the remainder,' the remainder that is in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי gives his source from the word 'the remainder' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller gives back what is left of the money that came into his hands. He received 100, not 200, so the field's higher value does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder, what is left over
That is in his hand, the money he actually got

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי דוסתאי, a rise in the field's value does not raise the redemption price, because the seller returns only what is left of the money he received.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same פסוק is read in two ways: רבי uses 'to the man' for the resale cases, and רבי דוסתאי uses 'the remainder' for a field that rose in value.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And he returns the remainder'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:27

phrases.english: — the remainder that is in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי דוסתאי raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The remainder' means what is left of the money in the seller's hand, so the original price is used.

steps.title: The field was sold for 200 and dropped to 100
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה brings the opposite of his earlier case. The field was sold for 200 and then lost value down to 100. How do we know the seller pays only by 100?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold it to him for 200, and it lost value and was worth only 100, how do we know the payment is figured only by 100?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה continues with a second case: this time the field goes down in value while the buyer holds it. He asks for the source that the seller pays only by the lower value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the field went up in value, and the seller still paid by the lower amount, the original 100. Now the field goes down, and again he wants the seller to pay the lower amount. Either way the seller comes out ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: It lost value (it went down in price)
One hundred (100 זוז)
We calculate (the redemption payment)

phrases.english: If he sold it to him for two hundred,
and it lost value and came to be worth one hundred,
from where do we know that we calculate only by one hundred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 19's case around: the value drops instead of rising.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that when the field loses value, the seller pays only by its present lower value.

steps.title: What remains in the land
steps.stepSummary: The same words 'and he returns the remainder' are read as 'what remains in the land,' meaning the field's present value. So he pays by 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'and he returns the remainder.' This means the remainder that is in the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה answers from the same פסוק he used in step 20, but this time he reads it as the value left in the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, 'העודף' meant what is left of the money the seller received. Here it also means what is left of the field's worth. The two readings together let the seller always pay by the lower amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder, what is left over
Land, the field itself

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, 'העודף' works both ways: what remains of the money, and what remains of the land's value. The seller pays whichever is lower.

phrases.english: As it says: 'And he returns the remainder'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:27

phrases.english: meaning the remainder that is in the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'העודף' is read as the value left in the land, so he pays only the present 100.

steps.title: How do רבי and רבי דוסתאי differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רבי and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in what case the views of רבי and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה would give different results. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views read the verses to help the seller, so it is not clear where they actually disagree. The גמרא wants a real case where the outcome changes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' is רבי from step 18 and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה from steps 19-22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views are laid out, the גמרא asks how they differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה would rule differently.

steps.title: Value went up, down, and up again
steps.stepSummary: They differ when the field was worth a lot at the first sale, dropped before the second sale, and then rose again before the seller redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where it went up in value, went down, and went up again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case where the price keeps changing: high at the first sale (200), low at the second sale (100), and high again (200) when the seller comes to redeem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, we count by the second buyer, who paid only 100. According to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, the payment is figured by the 200, using either what is left of the money first received or what is left of the land's present value. So in this case the two views give different payments.

keyTerms.meaning: It went up in value
It went down in price, became cheap

phrases.english: Where it went up in value, then went down, then went up again.
phrases.notes: It was high (200) at the first sale, low (100) at the second sale, and high again when the seller came to redeem it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when the value rose, fell before the second sale, and rose again: רבי counts by the second sale's 100, and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה counts by 200.

steps.title: Why read the verses to help the seller?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both views: how do we know to read the verses as a קולא for the seller? Maybe they should be read as a חומרא, against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know it is meant as a leniency? Maybe it is meant as a stringency!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on everything said so far. Every reading helped the seller, but why not read the same verses to make him pay more?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the man to whom he sold it' and 'the remainder' could each point to either the higher or the lower amount. Nothing yet tells us to always pick the one that is easier on the seller. This is a challenge to the basic direction of all the readings.

keyTerms.meaning: As a leniency, to make it easier
As a stringency, to make it harder
Perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is meant as a leniency?
phrases.notes: Easier for the seller, who is redeeming his field.

phrases.english: Maybe it is meant as a stringency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction shared by all the readings from both רבי and רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the redemption verses are read in favor of the seller.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words could just as easily be read to make the seller pay the higher amount.

steps.title: Learned from the redemption of an עבד עברי
steps.stepSummary: The word 'גאולה' (redemption) appears both here and by an עבד עברי. Since the Torah is lenient with the redeemer there, it is lenient here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: That should not enter your mind, because he learns 'redemption' and 'redemption' from a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a גזירה שוה: the same word, 'גאולה,' links redeeming a field to redeeming an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By an עבד עברי, the Torah makes it easier for him to be redeemed. Because the same word is used for the field, we apply the same easier approach to the seller who redeems his field. That is why all the readings go in the seller's favor.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind (that idea is wrong)
Redemption, buying back
A Jewish servant
Linking two passages through a shared word, so a law from one applies to the other

steps.whatToRemember: All the redemption calculations favor the seller, because 'גאולה' of a field is linked to 'גאולה' of an עבד עברי, where the Torah is lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the field is like a slave in every way. It only borrows one idea from the עבד עברי: that redemption is treated leniently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why every reading in this סוגיא, whether רבי's or רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה's, chooses the lower price for the seller.

phrases.english: Do not think that,
because he learns 'redemption' and 'redemption' from a Hebrew slave.
phrases.notes: Both passages use the same word: field, ויקרא 25:26; slave, ויקרא 25:48. That shared word lets us carry over the leniency.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּגָמַר גְּאוּלָּה גְּאוּלָּה מֵעֶבֶד עִבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה linking the field to a parallel case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses might be read against the seller, as a חומרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through the shared word 'גאולה,' the Torah's leniency toward redeeming an עבד עברי carries over to redeeming a field.

steps.title: How do we know the Torah is lenient with an עבד עברי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the Torah is lenient when an עבד עברי redeems himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by the Hebrew slave, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the foundation of the last answer. It asks how we know the Torah is lenient with an עבד עברי who redeems himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 learned the field case from the עבד עברי case through the shared word 'גאולה'. That only works if the עבד עברי case really is a קולא. So the גמרא now asks for proof of that.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)
A Jewish man sold as a slave for a set time
There (pointing to the other case)

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: 'There' is the עבד עברי case from the last step: how do we know the Torah is lenient with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the comparison used in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the redemption of an עבד עברי is calculated leniently, in his favor.

steps.title: If the slave's value went up, he pays by the original price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a slave sold for 100 who became worth 200 redeems himself based on the 100, learned from 'מכסף מקנתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If he was sold for 100 and rose in value to 200, how do we know we calculate only by the 100? Because it says 'from the money of his purchase.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Its first case: the slave became more valuable, but he still pays based on the lower price he was bought for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says he pays back 'from the money of his purchase', meaning the original sale price. That ignores his new, higher value, so the slave benefits.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of 100 זוז
Went up in value
We calculate (the redemption price)
'From the money of his purchase,' his original price

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
He was sold for a hundred, and he went up in value
and was now worth two hundred;
from where do we know that we calculate only from the hundred?
phrases.notes: This is the price he pays to go free early for the years he has left.

phrases.english: As it says: 'from the money of his purchase.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:51

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 27 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the slave's value rose, the redemption is still calculated by the lower original price, from 'מכסף מקנתו'.

steps.title: If the slave's value went down, he pays by the current value
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a slave sold for 200 who is now worth only 100 redeems himself based on the 100, learned from 'כפי שניו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was sold for 200 and dropped in value to 100, how do we know we calculate only by the 100? Because it says 'according to his years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case: the slave became less valuable. Here too he pays by the lower number, which is his current worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'according to his years' look at what his remaining years are worth now. Put together with step 28, the slave always pays by whichever value is lower. That is the קולא step 26 relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down in value
'According to his years,' his present worth for the years left

steps.whatToRemember: An עבד עברי who redeems himself always pays by the lower value. If his value went up, he pays by the original price. If it went down, he pays by the present value.

phrases.english: He was sold for two hundred, and he went down in value
and was now worth a hundred;
from where do we know that we calculate only from the hundred?
As it says: 'according to his years.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:52

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא. It covers the case where his value dropped.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the slave's value dropped, the redemption is calculated by the lower current value, from 'כפי שניו'.

steps.title: The same leniency applies to a slave sold to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says these פסוקים speak about a slave sold to a גוי, and uses a גזירה שוה on 'שכיר' to apply the same rule to a slave sold to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, that he is redeemed with the upper hand. From where do we know it for one sold to a Jew? The Torah says 'hired worker' and 'hired worker' for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices that these פסוקים are about a slave sold to a גוי. It shows that a slave sold to a Jew gets the same advantage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שכיר' appears in both sections of the Torah, by a slave sold to a גוי and by a slave sold to a Jew. A גזירה שוה links them, so the 'pay the lower value' rule carries over. That makes the leniency a general rule for every עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'His hand is on top,' meaning he has the advantage
Is redeemed (buys his freedom)
Hired worker
Learning one case from another because the Torah uses the same word in both

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the leniency true for every עבד עברי. That is why step 26 could use 'גאולה' to make field redemption lenient too.

phrases.english: And I only know this about a Hebrew slave
who was sold to a gentile,
that he is redeemed with the upper hand;
one sold to a Jew, from where do we know it?
The verse teaches: 'hired worker,' 'hired worker,'
phrases.notes: One 'שכיר' is in ויקרא 25:50 (sold to a גוי), and the other is in דברים 15:18 (sold to a Jew).

phrases.english: for a verbal analogy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶבֶד עִבְרִי הַנִּמְכָּר לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule from steps 28 and 29 and applies it to a slave sold to a Jew as well.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'שכיר' gives a slave sold to a Jew the same advantage of paying the lower value.

steps.title: אביי begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement of אביי, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. אביי is about to say something, and his words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here. The content of אביי's statement, and what it teaches, comes in the next lines of the גמרא.

phrases.english: אביי said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for the עבד עברי leniency is finished, a new statement from אביי begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only; אביי's ruling comes in the next lines.
